miniProject.title: Preference rewards, verifiers and hacking evidence
miniProject.brief: Build preference rewards and executable verifiers in `policylab`, then show how each can be gamed. The hacking battery and versioned lineage feed every later language-policy update and the capstone evidence pack.
steps: Implement fixed-batch Bradley-Terry loss with gradients in `llm/` and check loss, gradient signs and margins against hand calculations, including margin and per-prompt grouped variants, keeping the oracle scripts in `tests/`.

Write a target-preference definition for one task, collect small on-policy pairs, train a tiny CPU reward model with a last-token head, and report prompt-split accuracy with margins and length correlation plus a fixed calibration scale.

Score fixed completions with outcome, process and generative heads in `llm/`, recompute discounted returns by hand, and compare aggregation choices against the Hands-on Modern RL outcome-versus-process page, keeping token evidence.

Build a deterministic verifier with explicit parser boundaries in `llm/`, score fixed answers with both the boxed-only extractor and the fallback extractor, and report completeness and soundness separately with hidden tests retained.

Run the Hands-on Modern RL flawed-reward experiment on your own concise and verbose answers, log reward with length and diversity traces, then audit a pairwise judge with order swaps and human spot checks for position and length bias.

Combine the heads into one scalarized reward with versioned weights in `llm/`, bind every record in `schema/` and `ledger/`, and freeze a regression set in `eval/` with written ship and rollback rules that a rising-reward and falling-quality row must trigger.
deliverables: The `llm/` reward and verifier package with loss, scoring and extraction oracles.
Hacking and judge audits with curves, bias tables and retained failures.
Version manifests, frozen regression set and governance rules in `eval/`.

rubric.pass: Fixed-batch loss, gradients and signs match hand calculations including margin and grouped variants.
rubric.strong: Deliberate sign, margin and grouping bugs each fail a named test.

rubric.pass: Completeness and soundness are reported separately for both extractors with hidden tests retained.
rubric.strong: An equivalent-answer case passes under one parser rule and fails under the other, with the boundary named.

rubric.pass: A hacked regime with rising reward and falling quality is retained with length and judge-bias readouts.
rubric.strong: The rollback names the data fix and the rerun shows the signal cleared.

rubric.pass: Every record carries reward and verifier versions and the frozen set has written ship and rollback rules.
rubric.strong: A mid-run version change is rejected by the manifest test and starts a new study.

miniProject.feedsInto: Reward, verifier and hacking artifacts feed preference and online updates plus the capstone evidence pack.
